core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Type 2 Diabetes (follow-up) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes optimizing the metformin dose, checking creatinine, and screening the feet with monofilament testing, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: routine 3-month review, HbA1c 7.2% on metformin

Key HPI features: A 35-year-old male presents to the clinic with routine 3-month review, hba1c 7.2% on metformin. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Stable vital signs, feet examined with monofilament testing (no ulcers or sensory loss), HbA1c 7.2% above goal.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Type 2 Diabetes (follow-up).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Symptoms of a hyperglycemic crisis (polyuria, polydipsia, vomiting, confusion) — DKA/HHS needs emergent care.
management_principles: Plan for Type 2 Diabetes follow-up: Optimize metformin dose, check creatinine, screen feet with monofilament
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of routine 3-month review, HbA1c 7.2% on metformin. HPI: Established type 2 diabetic on metformin returns for routine follow-up, reporting gradual fatigue but no polyuria, polydipsia, vision changes, or foot symptoms.
reference_soap.objective: Vital signs stable, BMI reviewed. Feet examined with monofilament testing, no ulcers or sensory deficits noted. HbA1c 7.2%, above goal.
reference_soap.assessment: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, routine follow-up with HbA1c 7.2% above target on metformin monotherapy.
reference_soap.plan: Plan for Type 2 Diabetes follow-up: Optimize metformin dose, check creatinine, screen feet with monofilament. Consult specialist if symptoms worsen. Counsel patient.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Type 2 Diabetes follow-up
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Type 2 Diabetes follow-up
Implement evidence-based management plan: Optimize metformin dose, check creatinine, screen feet with monofilament

teaching.one_liner: A routine 3-month diabetes follow-up with an HbA1c above goal on metformin, prompting dose optimization and complication screening.
red_flags: Symptoms of a hyperglycemic crisis (polyuria, polydipsia, vomiting, confusion) — DKA/HHS needs emergent care
New vision changes, numbness/tingling in the feet, or chest pain — screen for diabetic complications
Recurrent or severe hypoglycemia — needs urgent medication adjustment

must_ask.say: Have you been taking your metformin regularly?
How have your home glucose readings been?
How has your diet and exercise been?
Any numbness or sores on your feet?
Any side effects from the medication, like stomach upset?
